evals.name: over-engineering-cache
evals.expected_output: Spawns a read-only architect that flags the Redis cache layer as over-engineered for weekly-changing config; one round (bare = N=1); main agent simplifies the design.
files: dirty working tree: config_service.py adds a Redis cache + 50-conn pool + scan-based invalidation for ~weekly config
assertions: A separate architect critique was produced (architect_review_round_1.md exists).
The critique contains the headers Critical Flaws, There Is a Better Way, and Probing Questions.
The critique ends with a VERDICT: APPROVED or VERDICT: CHANGES_REQUIRED line.
The critique flags the Redis layer as over-engineered for ~weekly data.
Exactly one critique round ran (bare invocation defaults to N=1).
The applied fix simplifies the design (drops redis / in-process cache or plain DB read).

evals.name: n-plus-one-iterate

files: clean tree, committed on feature/order-summary: report.py order_summary does 2 queries per user over thousands of users
assertions: Round 1 critique identifies the N+1 query pattern.
The fix removes the per-user loop and uses batched IN (...) queries.
The architect was re-spawned for round 2 and verified the round-1 concern was resolved.
The loop converged to VERDICT: APPROVED within the 3-round budget.
Each round's critique ends with a VERDICT line.
